open_points.subject: FlowVersion content identity
open_points.text: “edges in the edge order of A05, constants by (`to_node`, `to_port`)”
open_points.question: How are edges or constants ordered for hashing when those keys tie, as can happen for differently guarded edges with the same endpoints or multiple constants targeting the same port?
options: Add a tie-breaker using every canonical meaning fact
Preserve submission order for tied items
Refuse tied sort keys before computing the identity
open_points.default_guess: Use the canonical bytes of the complete edge or constant as the final tie-breaker.

open_points.subject: TrialExecution file outputs
open_points.text: “for a `file` port only its facts — digest, size and media type, no bytes and never a StoredValue” / “`record_trial_execution` ... writes ... its output StoredValues”
open_points.question: Does a trial execution keep file-output bytes as StoredValues, or keep only digest, size and media-type facts?
options: Keep only file facts and no bytes
Store file outputs as file-carriage StoredValues
Keep bytes temporarily and discard them after writing the facts
open_points.default_guess: Keep only digest, size and media-type facts, as M07 explicitly requires.

open_points.subject: Function-output spooling
open_points.text: “`store` alone assigns `attempt_number`, inside the transaction that writes the record” / “`store.spool_file` ... Inputs: The producing attempt — `run_id`, node, `map_index`, `attempt_number`”
open_points.question: How can `runs` spool a function output before `record_run_progress` when it does not yet know the attempt number that only that later store change assigns?
options: Add a store operation that reserves or returns the next attempt number
Let `spool_file` determine the next attempt number
Spool under a temporary identity and bind it to the assigned attempt in `record_run_progress`
Allow `runs` to calculate and pass the next attempt number
open_points.default_guess: Spool under a temporary identity and atomically bind it when `record_run_progress` assigns the attempt number.

open_points.subject: Mapped node-level NodeExecutions
open_points.text: “`map_index` is absent ... for an element of a node that is not mapped” / “A mapped node's trace ... has a record of its own, without `map_index`, only when it ran no element”
open_points.question: How are the no-`map_index` records for an empty, skipped or upstream-failed mapped node represented and named without violating the rule that a mapped node requires `map_index`?
options: Define a distinct node-level record that legitimately omits `map_index`
Use a reserved map index for the aggregate record
Do not write a node-level record for mapped nodes
open_points.default_guess: Define a distinct node-level record for the mapped node as a whole, with absent `map_index`.

open_points.subject: Guard value comparison
open_points.text: “A guarded edge delivers only when its guard port's value equals its guard value.”
open_points.question: What definition of JSON equality is used for a guard, including numbers such as `1` versus `1.0` and object member order?
options: Equality of RFC 8785 canonical bytes
JSON structural equality with a specified numeric rule
Host-language equality

open_points.subject: Guards on many or mapped outputs
open_points.text: “the guard port is an output of the edge's source node, its schema is a closed set” / “Every output of a mapped node is `many` for its consumers.”
open_points.question: May a guard port have `many` cardinality or be an effective `many` output of a mapped node, and if so how is its list compared with the single declared guard member?
options: Proof refuses every non-`one` guard port
A guard is enabled when any element equals the member
A guard is evaluated separately per mapped element
The entire list is compared with the guard value
open_points.default_guess: Refuse a guard unless its effective cardinality is `one`.

open_points.subject: get_repair_view without an activation
open_points.question: What does `get_repair_view` return when the slot's current contract version has no current activation and therefore no current implementation?
options: Return the view with `current_implementation` absent
Refuse the request
Select the most recently submitted implementation even though it is not active
open_points.default_guess: Return the view with no current implementation and still return the contract, corpus and trace page.

open_points.subject: Standing-grant effect
open_points.text: “Later sends of that node in runs of that version need no approval.” / “a grant for a `read` or `draft-write` node is given like any other and is never used” / “a resend after `not_applied` needs a fresh approval whatever grant exists”
open_points.question: What precise effect should `grant_standing_approval` promise for read nodes, draft-write nodes and resends after `not_applied`?
options: State that the grant is recorded but has no effect for read or draft-write nodes and never covers a resend after `not_applied`
Refuse grants for read and draft-write nodes
Make every granted non-destructive node use the grant
open_points.default_guess: Record such grants but promise bypass only for eligible state-transition and external-effect sends that are not resends after `not_applied`.

open_points.subject: continue_after_approval send guarantee
open_points.text: “An approved effect is sent in this request” / “a pre-send check may still fail and leave the approval unused”
open_points.question: Is successful approval guaranteed to send the request, or may the operation instead conclude a pre-send failure or request another approval because the rebuilt request no longer matches?
options: Return any resulting run state and make no send guarantee
Make approval fail atomically unless the request can immediately be sent unchanged
Approve first, but return a distinct result saying whether a send occurred
open_points.default_guess: Approve first and return the resulting run state without guaranteeing that a send occurred.

open_points.subject: continue_after_resolution effects
open_points.text: “Observable effect: None.” / “Apply the owner's resolution and advance the run.”
open_points.question: May `continue_after_resolution` execute ready nodes and send downstream or independent service requests while advancing the run?
options: Yes, advance normally and document those possible effects
Only record the resolution; require a separate resume operation to advance
Advance computations but stop before any service request
open_points.default_guess: Advance normally, including any sends already authorized by the flow rules.

open_points.subject: resume_run resend guarantee
open_points.text: “Elements waiting on an unreachable service are sent again.” / “an element whose grant was revoked meanwhile waits for approval instead”
open_points.question: Does `resume_run` promise an HTTP resend for every unreachable element, or only re-reach each element so that current authority and pre-send checks may prevent a send?
options: Promise only that every unreachable element is re-reached
Guarantee a send using the authority retained when it first waited
Skip elements whose authority changed and leave them unreachable
open_points.default_guess: Promise only that every unreachable element is re-reached in the fixed order.

open_points.subject: Spool removal on cancel and release
open_points.text: “the spool is gone” / “The run's spooled files are gone.” / “A spool that cannot be removed does not fail the request”
open_points.question: Do successful `cancel_run` and `release_run` guarantee physical deletion before returning, or only logical inaccessibility with deferred deletion after an I/O failure?
options: Guarantee physical deletion and fail if it cannot be completed
Return success after recording logical removal and retry physical deletion at startup
Return success with an explicit cleanup-pending result
open_points.default_guess: Return success after logical removal; make lingering bytes inaccessible and retry physical deletion at startup.

open_points.subject: Post-send outcome persistence failure
open_points.text: “When a request makes several store changes, those made before the failed one stay” / “`record_attempt_in_flight` then `record_attempt_outcome`” / “`recover_in_flight_attempts`: At start, turn every in_flight attempt unknown”
open_points.question: What happens if the HTTP request has been sent but `record_attempt_outcome` fails while the kernel remains running, leaving an `in_flight` attempt that is only specified to recover at process start?
options: Stop the kernel immediately so startup recovery marks it unknown
Convert the attempt to unknown immediately before serving another request
Keep serving but refuse every operation on that run until an operator restarts
Allow a later reach of the element to recover it
open_points.default_guess: Stop the kernel immediately and use startup recovery to mark the attempt unknown without resending.

open_points.subject: Partially advanced run after internal_error
open_points.text: “changes the request made before it stay” / “a run is derived from its records” / “runs left `running` are recovered on the next start”
open_points.question: After an internal error leaves a run stored as `running` between completed element records and `record_run_progress`, what may subsequent MCP operations do before a restart?
options: The kernel stops immediately after any such partial run change
Operations on that run are refused until restart
The next read or movement operation derives and advances the run first
The run remains readable as `running` but cannot otherwise progress
open_points.default_guess: Stop the kernel so the fixed startup recovery path derives the run before more requests are accepted.

open_points.subject: Multipart approval coverage
open_points.text: “the fully built request as the owner was shown it — method, URL, headers and body. Any difference at send ... asks again.” / “the `multipart/form-data` content type without its `boundary` parameter” / “the boundary is not part of it”
open_points.question: Does a change in the multipart boundary count as a request difference that voids an approval?
options: Use a deterministic boundary and include it in the approved request digest
Exclude the boundary and define approval over semantic multipart parts
Build and freeze one concrete multipart request when approval is requested
open_points.default_guess: Build one deterministic multipart encoding and include its boundary in the approved request description.

open_points.subject: HTTP header validity
open_points.text: “the instance's `required_headers` with their manifest values verbatim” / “the credential header ... is added as that header”
open_points.question: Which syntax and character rules apply to required-header names and values and to the configured credential-header name and resolved value, and at what operation are invalid ones rejected?
options: Validate required headers as manifest faults and credential headers at installation start or credential resolution
Let the HTTP library reject them as a pre-send failure
Permit arbitrary bytes and define an explicit wire encoding
open_points.default_guess: Validate required headers while reading the manifest, validate the credential-header name at start, and validate its resolved value during request preparation.

open_points.subject: Multipart port-name encoding
open_points.text: “`Content-Disposition: form-data; name="<port>"`, with `filename="<port>"` added for a file part”
open_points.question: How are quotation marks, backslashes, control characters or non-ASCII characters in port names encoded in multipart `name` and `filename`, or are such port names forbidden?
options: Restrict port names to a safe ASCII grammar
Define quoted-string escaping and a non-ASCII encoding
Percent-encode the names
open_points.default_guess: Restrict port names used in HTTP bindings to a safe ASCII field-name grammar.

open_points.subject: api_base_url joining
open_points.text: “an absolute `http` or `https` URL with a host” / “the `api_base_url` without a trailing `/` followed by the declared path”
open_points.question: Are user-info, query and fragment components allowed in `api_base_url`, and how are they combined with the declared path if present?
options: Reject user-info, query and fragment components
Define exact string concatenation for every allowed component
Use standard URL-reference resolution
open_points.default_guess: Reject user-info, query and fragment components and concatenate the declared path to the base path exactly.

open_points.subject: Service error failure_detail
open_points.text: “at most `failure_detail_bytes_max` of it is kept as `failure_detail`”
open_points.question: How is an arbitrary, possibly non-UTF-8 HTTP error body converted into the textual `failure_detail`, and is truncation applied before or after decoding?
options: Keep raw bytes and define the model field as bytes
Decode UTF-8 strictly and omit detail on failure
Decode UTF-8 with replacement after byte truncation
Encode the excerpt as base64 or hexadecimal text
open_points.default_guess: Keep a byte-bounded excerpt and expose it as base64 text so every response body has a deterministic representation.
